flow.costPlain: The direct cost of delivering Arm's designs and support — tiny next to revenue, which is why gross margin is 95.6%. It includes $8M of share-based pay.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Designing new processors and platform technology; the GAAP figure includes $139M of share-based pay (paying staff in shares). Engineering headcount rose 20% year over year. Non-GAAP R&D was $293M, up 9% year over year.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: Selling and running the company; the GAAP figure includes $49M of share-based pay. Non-GAAP SG&A was $166M, up 20% year over year as non-engineering headcount rose 13% and the prior year benefited from a one-time bad-debt reversal.

opex.name: Disposal, restructuring and other
opex.note: Small restructuring, disposal and other operating costs.

follow100Note: License ($42.96) and royalty ($57.04) revenue make up the $100. Direct costs took $4.37; R&D took $52.43 and SG&A $26.21, plus $0.73 of disposal and restructuring costs — leaving $16.26 before other items. Interest and other gains added $1.58, equity investments lost $0.12, and a $59M tax expense took $7.16. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Arm beat its own Q3 guidance ($720–800M revenue); it guided Q4 FY24 revenue of $850–900M and raised full-year FY24 revenue guidance to $3,155–3,205M.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: diluted, vs $0.18 a year ago; non-GAAP $0.29

kpis.label: Royalty revenue
kpis.note: +11% YoY — a record, on wider Armv9 adoption

otherDetail: Other items added $12M: $28M of net interest income, partly offset by a $15M other non-operating loss and a $1M loss from equity investments. Tax was a $59M expense — a 40.4% effective rate — so it took from profit instead of adding to it.
pngFooterNote: Record revenue; hiring costs cut profit in half.

segments.name: License and other revenue
segments.note: Fees for licensing Arm chip designs, plus support and related services; up 18% YoY on multiple high-value long-term license agreements as companies invest in Arm-based technology for AI across all end markets.

segments.name: Royalty revenue
segments.note: A cut of every chip shipped with Arm technology inside; up 11% YoY to a record as Armv9 chips — which command higher royalty rates, typically at least double Armv8 — spread wider, with strong growth in smartphones (AI-enabled Armv9 handsets) and cloud servers, plus automotive driver-assistance chips. IoT/embedded was flat.

takeaways.text: Revenue rose 14% to a record $824M, above guidance ($720–800M), on record royalty revenue of $470M (+11%) and license revenue of $354M (+18%) from multiple high-value long-term deals signed as companies invest in AI. The pipeline looks strong too: remaining performance obligations were $2,433M (+38% YoY) and annualized contract value $1,160M (+15% YoY, +5% QoQ). Arm guided Q4 FY24 revenue of $850–900M and raised full-year FY24 revenue guidance to $3,155–3,205M (from $2,960–3,080M).
takeaways.title: Record revenue, above guidance

takeaways.text: Royalty revenue hit a record $470M as Armv9 chips, which carry royalty rates typically at least double Armv8, spread into more markets: Armv9 now contributes around 15% of royalty revenue, up from around 10% last quarter. Smartphone royalties grew strongly on the market recovery and AI-enabled Armv9 handsets, cloud servers grew on market-share gains, and automotive grew on driver-assistance chips (microcontrollers slowed). IoT/embedded was flat on last year's inventory correction. Customers reported shipping 7.7 billion Arm-based chips in the September quarter, taking the cumulative total to 280.3 billion.
takeaways.title: Armv9 is lifting what Arm earns per chip

takeaways.text: GAAP operating profit fell 45% to $134M (a 16.3% margin) after operating expenses rose 45% to $654M: R&D was $432M (52.4% of revenue) on 20% engineering headcount growth, and total share-based pay was $196M ($8M in cost of sales, $139M in R&D, $49M in SG&A). Non-GAAP operating profit was $338M, up 17%, a 41.0% margin. Net income of $87M (vs $182M a year ago) compares with non-GAAP net income of $305M (+36%). Free cash flow was $251M, and $724M over the trailing twelve months (+63%).
takeaways.title: Record revenue, thinner profit

verdict: Arm's revenue hit a record $824M, up 14% and above its own guidance, on record royalty revenue — but net income fell 52% to $87M as hiring and share-based pay pushed operating costs up 45%.
